title: Adaptive per-kernel span sampling and prefill/decode timeline correlation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: produce a low-overhead, high-fidelity observability surface that ties per-kernel execution metrics (latency, flops, occupancy) to high-level request phases (prefill vs decode) and the scheduling decisions that picked each kernel variant. This ticket implements adaptive span sampling, an NVTX naming scheme, and trace/span correlation so engineers can: 1) attribute token-level latency regressions to specific kernels and scheduling choices, 2) measure frequency and cost of kernel fallbacks, and 3) validate prefill/ decode overlap and its impact on tail latency.

Outcomes: instrumentation merged to runtime main, dashboards with per-kernel histograms and prefill/decode timeline visualizations, a lightweight sampling runtime mode for host-level benchmarks, and a short doc that codifies NVTX/trace naming and sampling policy for on-call and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits NVTX ranges and trace spans with deterministic names that include kernel_variant, op_type, model_family, and request_phase
Adaptive sampling limits overhead to <3% p95 latency regression on stress tests (internal perf harness)
Prefill vs decode timelines can be correlated in traces and shown in dashboard with per-kernel latency heatmap
Dashboards show per-kernel p50/p95/p99 latency, invocation count, and fallback rate over 30d
Automated tests validate NVTX range nesting for prefill->decode handoff and KV-cache warmup sequences
updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Observability, and SRE. Agreed to prioritize low-overhead sampling; initial design doc drafted (link in 'links').
2026-03-02: Prototype NVTX naming scheme: runtime.kernel.{model}.{op}.{variant}.{phase}. Added examples and reserved tokens for sequence_length and batch_id. Shared with infra for feedback.

2026-03-05: Microbenchmark of naive full-span emission showed 12% p95 regression under 8x concurrency. Decided on adaptive sampling strategy: deterministic 1-in-N baseline + burst capture on anomaly triggers (latency spike or error rate).

2026-03-07: Implemented span header propagation to associate CUDA kernel launches with higher-level request_id and phase. Added lightweight per-kernel counters to avoid expensive string operations on hot path.

2026-03-09: Design review with PM and Observability. Feedback: expose sampling knobs via config file and runtime flags; add 'always-capture' for canary customers. Action: add flags and document defaults.
2026-03-11: Internal PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345 — contains NVTX wrappers, sampling manager, and tests. Performance CI running (expected pass 2026-03-13).

2026-03-12: Found edge case in kernel fallback accounting where short-lived kernels (<50us) were undercounted due to timer resolution. Interim fix: coalesce short spans into a summary counter. Planning follow-up to use high-resolution timers in CUDA event-based path.
notes: Sampling strategy: base_rate=1/100 (config); adaptive window increases sampling to 1/10 for 5s after p95>target or any kernel error. Burst capture writes full spans to ephemeral store for 1 minute then samples down.
NVTX naming: use compact tokens to minimize string allocs on hot path. Map to human-readable via dashboard lookup table. Example short name: r.kv.kAttention.q8.prefill

Trace correlation: include numeric request_id and phase enum in span attributes rather than long strings to reduce serialization cost. Use span ids to join with per-kernel counters in aggregation job.
Performance trade-offs: full per-span capture is precise but too costly at scale. The hybrid approach keeps overhead bounded while enabling deep diagnosis when anomalies occur.
Follow-ups: add GPU-side CUDA event aggregation path to get sub-50us resolution for short kernels; add sampling telemetry to Dedicated customers opt-in control plane.
